Present-tense be (is/are/am) and ordinary lexical verbs do not drive it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lighthouse at Greyrock Point had stood for almost a century before the harbor board voted to automate its lamp, and the keepers who tended its brass lenses kept meticulous logs of every storm, every passing steamer, every gull strike against the glass. Winter gales tore shingles from the oil house, summer fog swallowed the breakwater, and still the light turned through each night while clerks in the distant port city tallied coal deliveries, rope purchases, paint requisitions, and the endless petitions from fishermen who claimed the channel markers had drifted. Committees met, surveyors redrew the shoal charts, insurers raised their premiums after two schooners grounded on the outer reef, and the town council argued for months about who should pay for a new foghorn. Rival shipowners accused each other of bribing the pilots, newspaper editors printed angry letters about neglected buoys, and a retired captain published a memoir insisting the currents had shifted since his youth. Engineers arrived with theodolites, divers inspected the granite foundation, masons repointed the tower joints, and apprentices hauled fresh oil up the spiral stairs each dusk. The archives filled with tide tables, wreck reports, salvage claims, weather diaries, and correspondence with the ministry, while schoolchildren toured the gallery and sketched the great Fresnel lens in their notebooks. After years of quarrels between the port authority, the merchants guild, and the coastal parishes over duties, repairs, salvage rights, and the wages of the keepers, the exhausted delegates finally gathered in the drafty customs house one rainy November evening. The agreement was signed after months of tense negotiation over the foghorn. Afterwards the harbor settled into an uneasy routine, the new horn boomed across the bay, the keepers grumbled about the noise, the gulls scattered, the tide kept its own counsel, and the light kept turning through fog and frost while the town below slept.
